column1: # THE PURSE -- append-only. FUNDS ARE DERIVED: `python tools/ledger.py`.
# `delta` is a number and `unit` names what it is a number OF. Two columns on
# purpose: 1e has five coin types with real exchange rates, and WHICH COIN is
# sometimes the interesting fact. The day-39 anchor records '28 ep off the orc
# bodies, +14' -- the electrum survives only in that prose, because the
# conversion happened before the column existed. Positive in, negative out;
# 0.1 gp = 1 s.p. tools/ledger.py sums in gp.
# `asset` MUST name a row in campaign/assets.tsv and tools/log.py refuses a row
# without one. That requirement IS the double entry: five errors in this
# campaign were purchases recorded only as a sentence inside the notes column of
# the funds row, with no item row anywhere --
#     the two carts     40 days unrecorded
#     the two mules     ditto
#     the small goods   357 gp, 17 days untracked and never rolled
#     six 50-ft ropes   11 days, while the rope row still said 2
#     dragon scales     carried as unsold long after they were sold
# You cannot write a money row here without naming what the money was for.
# *** WHY THERE IS AN ANCHOR AT DAY 39 ***
# This file was reconstructed on 2026-09-11 from the 4,910-character notes blob
# on the `funds` row of inventory.tsv. FROM DAY 39 ONWARD THE BLOB RECONCILES
# figure the inventory row carries and the figure the tools compute. Every one
# of those movements is a row below.
# BEFORE DAY 39 IT DOES NOT RECONCILE. The day-34 chain (26.1 -> 265.1, less
# 115.5 of outfitting, less 3.2 to Coll, less 18 for Ista's kit) lands about a
# gold piece away from the day-35 opening figure of 150.6, and the blob does not
# say where the difference is. THAT IS THE FINDING, not a failure: a running
# total kept in prose stopped being reconcilable somewhere around day 34 and
# nobody could have known. Inventing eight rows to close a 1 gp gap would put
# false precision into an append-only log, so days 1-38 are one anchor carrying
# the narrative, exactly as the day-39 XP anchor does in encounters.tsv.
# An `anchor` row SETS the purse outright. Everything else adds.

ANCHOR: 595 gp 6 sp. Days 1-38 in one row because the prose blob stops reconciling around day 34 (see header). What it records: 211 gp 6 sp on departure for expedition 6, plus receipts that came in while the party was underground -- ~+312 the day-37 market on the small goods, ~+60 the tool line under Hask, +20 the last iron and salt AT COST, +14 for 28 ep off the orc bodies = 617 gp 6 sp; then LESS 22 gp for Ista's kit on day 39, which this row had never been debited and which the player caught. Earlier landmarks inside the anchor: day 34 receipts +80 iron/salt at cost and +159 the tool line; day-34 outfitting 114 gp 15 sp (10 oil flasks, five daggers, backpack, waterskin, keg and spigot, 18 person-weeks of iron rations); 3 gp 2 sp to Coll for wage arrears; 18 gp Ista's kit; day 35 +61 including Marrow's last ten pair of shears at 26 gp, which Hask UNDERSOLD by nine gold. HASK'S RING-FENCED SEVENTH of the tool line (~36 gp) is NOT in this figure and never has been.
The Draycot licence paid in coin on the table, Ottir witnessing. 25 gp a year for three years, backdated to Michaelmas last. articles.md art. 10

Small-goods receipts for days 38-54 that had never been rolled at the time: 26 (day-44 market) + 21 (day-51 market) + 14 (counter trade). Entered retroactively 2026-09-07, scale anchored by Wend's own day-48 statement that only half had sold, which OVERRIDES the dice
The vial named as REALGAR by Trebb the dyer and sold to the church's limner at Marchford. Valued 45 on 3d6=13; sold 35
The dye to Trebb AT COST, all of it, cash. Reaction 41 -- articles.md's first finding: at cost is a discount and a discount is a gift wearing a trade's clothes

The remaining small goods to OSSERY the mercer, blue shutters, at dusk on market day. HASK SOLD IT and did not undersell, holding his number through two silences. THE LINE CLOSES: 573 gp on 357 gp of cost

Paid at Lyde's door: 25 gp premium plus 6 gp first quarter's board of a year for Meg and Tibb, at 1 gp/month/head (DMG p.28's porter at 1 gp a month WITH quarters). OWING: 18 gp in three further quarterly instalments, next about day 152
Eleven shillings LENT to Dill for his tools -- a LOAN, entered as a debt at his own insistence, repayable out of his first month. He asked for it to be written that way

Toller's FULL valuation for Zelligar's laboratory apparatus, paid the moment he was shown Master Wace's receipt, which recites the contents of Dave's letter. His day-42 condition DISCHARGED after twenty-three days. Over a thousand gold for the first time
Marchford lodging never charged at the time: 8 people, 2 nights, house rule 1 gp/person/night. Booked day 67 when the omission was found
Eight person-weeks of STANDARD rations at 3 gp. Standard, not iron, deliberately -- iron exists to keep a month and a three-day trip does not

SIX 50-ft ropes at 4 s.p. One of the two old ropes was chewed more than halfway through on exp.6 and the plan put eight people on brake lines behind 460 lb. *** THE ROPE ROW STILL SAID 2 FOR ELEVEN DAYS AFTER THIS. This row and the corrected inventory line are the fix ***

First half of 58 gp for the 36-gallon SD cask. Holt named it off the bung without tapping it -- strong stock ale, thirty years and not turned. TWENTY-EIGHT GOLD IS STILL OWING in his own hand against the cask as he draws it, written unasked. That is loop L010, not a receivable in this file

FOUR person-weeks of STANDARD rations at 3 gp, bought the evening before expedition 9. Eight people for seven days is 8 person-weeks; the store held 4.5 (2.5 iron + 2 standard), so this brings it to 8.5 -- seven and a half days for eight. Standing order from the party: EAT THE OLD ONES FIRST, which is right, because standard rations do not keep a month and the day-67 packets are eleven days old while the IRON keeps and is therefore the reserve
TORSAT'S WEEK. Seven nights' bed and board at the house rule of 1 gp/person/night while he serves the DMG p.82 week. Paid up front so nobody has to remember it on day 87

EXPEDITION 10 FOOD. Four person-weeks of standard at 3 gp, bought the morning they turned round. Seven in the field -- Torsat invalid at the Inn, Hask still on the wool road -- so four person-weeks plus the 2.6 already held is about five days for seven, with the 2.5 person-weeks of IRON left untouched as the reserve

TWENTY-NINE COPPER off the two dead kobolds. MM treasure type J individually, 11 and 18. 29 cp = 0.29 gp at 100 cp to the gold -- the smallest sum this campaign has ever logged, and logged anyway because a rule that is skipped when the number is small is not a rule
DELLIE'S WEEK, five nights to day 88 at the house rate of 1 gp/person/night. SHARING TORSAT'S ROOM at her own request -- the rate is per person, not per room

THE WOOL PARTY'S BUY, day 73-83, ten days out. 36 tods at the published 8 gp floor. *** NOT THE PARTY'S MONEY AND DOES NOT MOVE THE PURSE *** -- Wend's venture money. This row exists only to count the party's EXPOSURE against art.7's 500 gp seasonal guarantee. Player's ruling 2026-09-15: track the cap, not the book; Wend's ledger is REPORTED, NOT INSPECTED

FOOD TO COOK, not packed rations -- the player's standing method since the Ludbury road: buy what can be prepared on the way and share the work. Ista taught the camp cooking last time and teaches the rest this time. Two person-weeks' worth of raw food at roughly 4 gp -- cheaper than the 3 gp/person-week of prepared standard rations because it is flour, bacon, onions and a sack of oats rather than packets

THE FORTY JARS SOLD TO TREBB at his own figure of 7 gp, WITHOUT SHOPPING THE TANNER HE HAD JUST NAMED. Dave's standing instruction from the road: he has helped this party repeatedly and for nothing -- named the vial as realgar on day 59 in his own yard with nobody exposed, and named all forty of these today for nothing. The party could have taken Toller's answer and walked it round the corner to a man in a different trade. IT DID NOT

A THIRD LIGHT RIDING HORSE AND TACK, bought at Marchford so somebody can ride to Fenn's while the carts stay put. 25 gp the horse plus 11 gp 5 sp tack -- THE SAME PRICE AND THE SAME PLACE as the light bay bought here on day 59 for Dellie, which is the figure this campaign has already paid and is therefore the figure it pays
